transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support. My name is Ryan. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Ryan. I booked a day off unpaid work today for an S-Net fiber broadband installation at our new cottage, but your contractor turned up, stared at a fallen tree branch resting on the telegraph pole line, announced he wasn't qualified to prune trees, and immediately drove away without connecting anything! I am furious!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open the contractor installation notes for your new connection docket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My mobile contact number on the work docket is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero eight one two.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please hold while I access the national Openreach field scheduling portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you still there, Ryan? The line went completely silent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, apologies for the silence. The field portal indicates that installation work order ORD-88210-F was closed by the contractor with code Tree Obstruction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The oak branch is literally pencil-thin and could be pushed aside with a broom handle! Leaving us without internet when both my partner and I work remotely is unacceptable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me examine the external line plant photos uploaded by the contractor to the job record.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We specifically scheduled our home move around having high-speed broadband live today so we wouldn't fall behind on client deadlines.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The photograph clearly shows the overhead lightweight dropwire severed completely where the branch snapped across the span.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the dropwire is physically cut, not merely obstructed! Why didn't the technician just splice a fresh length of fiber cable into the house?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Standard residential provisioning engineers are not certified or equipped to perform overhead high-level aerial drops or tree clearance near high-voltage utility poles.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then S-Net needs to dispatch an emergency specialized heavy civils crew with a cherry picker immediately to string the replacement cable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me review the contractor dispatch availability matrix across the Gloucestershire district.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We cannot wait two weeks without connectivity while remote consulting files are due.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, your registered contact telephone number is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero eight one two?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly my mobile number. You can reach me on that number at any time of day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the optical network terminal wall bracket and internal customer splice point already mounted inside your hallway?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the previous homeowner had an S-Net box mounted on the skirting board next to the power socket, with four small indicator lights.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you look at that internal optical box on the skirting board, are any of the front status LEDs illuminated?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The power light is solid green, but the optical PON light is flashing red and the LAN light is dark.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A flashing red PON indicator indicates zero optical carrier light reaching the receiver photodiode from the distribution splitter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Which makes total sense if the aerial cable is hanging snapped in half across the hedgerow outside!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you have clear line of sight from the eaves of your cottage roof to the telegraph pole situated across the lane?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, there is direct line of sight between our gable wall and the wooden pole, apart from that one snapped branch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please hold while I check whether an expedited aerial civils crew can be scheduled this week.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ryan, are you still on the line? It feels like the call keeps getting dropped.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I am back. The civils scheduling queue is fully booked across Gloucestershire for the next fourteen working days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fourteen working days?! That is nearly three entire weeks without broadband! How can you possibly expect paying subscribers to endure three weeks with zero internet?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under standard residential terms of service, aerial civils repairs require routine engineering scheduling windows.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you not escalate this to a regional operations manager or log an emergency service ticket under vulnerable remote workers?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I do not have managerial authority to override the fourteen-day regional civils backlog, so you will need to re-book online via the customer portal next month if the slot remains unavailable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an utterly useless response! You are telling me to just sit in an empty cottage with no internet and re-book online using non-existent broadband?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Company operating guidelines prevent frontline agents from booking out-of-area contractor teams without regional director sign-off.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So S-Net is essentially abandoning us on move-in day after taking our upfront setup fee and running credit checks!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The upfront installation fee remains on the pending account until successful physical service activation is confirmed on the wholesale radius server.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can S-Net at least supply an unlimited 4G mobile Wi-Fi dongle or credit our mobile data SIMs so we can work tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mobile broadband backup dongles are only provided for corporate business tier accounts, not residential tariffs under our current commercial product guidelines.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Every competitor in the United Kingdom provides emergency 4G backup when their installation fails on day one!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Residential accounts can tether personal smartphones to access cellular data subject to standard network data caps and carrier throttling.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our mobile data signal with our current phone network only gets one bar of fluctuating 3G or 4G inside this thick stone cottage.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Placing the smartphone near an upstairs dormer window often improves cellular data reception through Cotswold stone walls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Balancing a mobile phone on an upstairs window sill while running client video presentations is hardly a professional business solution for multi-gigabyte video conferencing calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented on the ticket that the aerial dropwire is fractured due to fallen timber and requires two-man high-level cherry picker access with local authority traffic control permissions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does replacing a snapped overhead dropwire across a narrow country lane require temporary road closure permits from Gloucestershire County Council?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When overhead cabling spans public vehicular carriageways, contractor health and safety rules mandate highway traffic management signage or lane closure permits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Which explains why the standard solo technician just took one look and drove away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Standard provisioning vans are only equipped with single-stage extension ladders certified up to six meters.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And that wooden telegraph pole across the hedge is at least nine or ten meters tall.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, joint-user distribution poles shared with electrical infrastructure strictly require bucket truck hydraulic platforms.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the formal reference number for this failed installation docket so I can track it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The installation docket reference number is FLT-77291-C.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: FLT-77291-C. I will keep that noted down for when I file a formal complaint with Ofcom and the communications ombudsman.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ticket notes will be accessible to whichever field crew eventually receives the regional dispatch assignment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our previous broadband with our old provider at our previous flat was ninety megabits and never dropped once, so we had never experienced anything like this before.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fiber to the cabinet connections rely on buried copper lines rather than overhead aerial spans that are vulnerable to tree branches.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I suppose buried cables don't snap when an autumn breeze blows an oak twig.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: External physical aerial drops across rural lanes will always carry higher susceptibility to environmental storm damage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If a tree branch falls again next winter, does that mean another three-week wait for a cherry picker?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once the replacement heavy-duty armored overhead dropwire is tensioned, it features reinforced steel messenger wires designed to withstand significant mechanical strain.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: At least the replacement cable will be somewhat stronger and less prone to snapping.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have verified that the installation order FLT-77291-C is queued in the regional engineering civils pool and the initial dispatch notes are saved. Does that answer all of your questions regarding the installation status today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You haven't resolved the three-week delay or sent an emergency dongle, but you've explained the status. I will escalate this with executive complaints. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Have a good afternoon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
